title: Syntagma sacrae theologiae (Liber I Cap. 6 densify complete)
author: Ludwig Crocius
edition: Syntagma sacrae theologiae (Bremen: Berthold Villerian, 1636). VD17 14:684303C. SLUB id335860389. Liber I Cap. 6 De sacrae Scripturae claritate COMPLETE (PHYS mid-238–244 before Cap. 7).
blurb: Ludwig Crocius — Book I Chapter 6 On Sacred Scripture's clarity, from the 1636 Bremen Latin. Densify COMPLETE (PHYS mid-238–244): clarity defined so saving faith and manners can be surely known; catholic ASSERTIO that saving dogmas are plain; eleven reasons (Scripture's witness, lamp, Spirit's promise, command to search, Bereans, fathers, Scripture's end, God revealing, prophets/Apostles, revealed dogmas, style); partial obscurity admitted with six reasons God willed it; conditioned and sufficient perspicuity for those who read decently; Cap. 6 close that Scripture alone is God's certain and infallible testimony. Cap. 7 On Scripture's sense and interpretation begins PHYS 245; Cap. 5 complete; the rest of the Syntagma remains.
era_note: Crocius wrote in the early seventeenth century as Reformed professor at the illustrious school of Bremen. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. The 1636 Villerian folio is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
